kb_proposals: A topology passed as an argument of type TopologicalSpace α is a LOCAL INSTANCE for every later binder and every `have`: `δ : α ≃ₜ α`, `deckGroup`, `connectedComponentIn` silently use it. Wrap it (`structure GX.WrappedTop α where top : TopologicalSpace α`) and write `@nhds _ T.top`; prove explicit-topology versions of mathlib lemmas by `letI := t; exact …` (GX.mem_nhds_iff_of and siblings in SingularII/Models).

Dot notation on a structure field of an explicit-topology Prop (`hT.isPortly.dense x`, `h.mono`, `hc.comp`) re-synthesizes the instance and fails with 'synthesized … not definitionally equal'; use `@IsPortly.dense _ T _ h` or a `letI` wrapper lemma.

To glue a topology defined by neighbourhood filters, `TopologicalSpace.mkOfNhds` + `nhds_mkOfNhds` (pure ≤ n, and s ∈ n a → ∀ᶠ y in n a, s ∈ n y) is far cheaper than a generateFrom: GX.chartTop/GX.nhds_chartTop.

Uniqueness of lifts into a maximal covering: maps continuous on an open set, with the same projection and regular over a dense preconnected open part, agreeing at one regular point, agree (GX.eqOn_maxBranched_of_base_eq); with regular transitivity they differ by a deck transformation (GX.exists_deck_eqOn_of_base_eq).
Identifiers with Latin-1 letters (Û, V̂, Ẑ) are rejected by the parser ('expected token'); Greek and letterlike symbols are fine.

A quotient topology through non-injective maps is cheap with mkOfNhds: put n y := map Ψ_y (𝓝 f_y) for a chosen preimage; the two mkOfNhds conditions need only that n (Ψ v) = map Ψ (𝓝 v) for every v, which is the Galois property of Ψ (GX.descNhds_eq, GX.nhds_descTop) — no openness of Ψ is needed up front, it follows.

Galoisianity of a sub-covering V̂ → Û between maximal coverings, without building it as a branched covering: move a regular point near v₁ to one near v₂ by a deck transformation (regular transitivity + a path-lifting surjectivity onto the regular part), then pin the singular point with the discreteness of the q-fibre (GX.IsChartDescent.exists_deck).
Beware python str.replace on Lean files: an anchor like '\nend DescTop' also matches '\nend DescTopHelpers'; assert the count is 1.

A theorem binder (h : P) elaborated AFTER a binder {T : TopologicalSpace α} uses T as the instance for α inside P (IsGaloisian, ≃ₜ, JoinedIn all silently pick T): order such binders BEFORE T, or write @JoinedIn _ (weakTopMax …), and build anonymous-constructor witnesses with `1`/expected types rather than Homeomorph.refl _ (GX.IsTamifyingTopology.nhds_eq_of_finite_stab).

Transporting a path to a coarser topology: @Path.mk α t' x y (@ContinuousMap.mk unitInterval α _ t' (fun i => γ i) (@Continuous.mk … fun s hs => @Continuous.isOpen_preimage … (TopologicalSpace.le_def.1 h s hs))) …; dot notation (γ.continuous.comp) re-synthesizes the wrong instance (GX.joinedIn_of_le_tamNec).

theo:local_virt_tame: the obstruction of its general case is intrinsic (GX.not_isVirtuallyTame_of_forall_not_joinedIn); a counterexample must kill, in a model, a local loop at a singular point not generated by meridians of finite-local-degree strata (those are forced into every T_α-neighbourhood by (A)+(C), GX.IsTamifyingTopology.nhds_eq_of_finite_stab).

Postcomposing a branched covering with a base homeomorphism: GX.IsBranchedCovering.homeomorph_comp (SingularII/Models) — spread by IsSpread.comp (of_isInducing h), completeness by SpreadEnd.map along h.symm and SpreadEnd.map_apply with V := h⁻¹' W, ord loci by image_ordX/Y_of_homeomorph (Homeomorph.refl E) h; branching locus GX.IsPossiblyBranchedOver.homeomorph_comp.

To map a maximal covering Ṽ of an open V onto a component Û of p⁻¹(U) over a chart φ : U ≅ V: branched_covering_restriction for Û → U, postcompose with φ, maxBranched_universal for V (the subtype), then fix the image of a prescribed point with a deck transformation of Ṽ (maxBranched_isGaloisian_cc; reg V slsc in V) — GX.isDescendingChartMap_of_section.
`set C := … ` AFTER an `obtain ⟨R, …⟩` whose type mentions C's body shadows R by a copy; do the `set` first, then the `obtain` (GX.isDescendingChartMap_of_homeomorph).

The ledger reads bold marks only in the first 4000 characters of the FILE (tools/ledger.py lean_index); WP-40c's def:topological_spaces_continuous_map mark sat at character 5510 and was invisible — put every marked bullet first, compact, and move long partial-row details below.

An open connected V of a model with sing V ⊆ S_α is an X_A-manifold via the chart (⊤ : Opens V) ≃ₜ V (GX.opensTopHomeo, GX.opensModelChart); IsAEMorphism through isAEMorphism_of_val_comp and the composite of two isAEMorphism_opensSingular_val.

A tamifying topology can be produced by making the model geometry X equal to the maximal covering with the desired topology: take X := the target space with a 'thin' topology at the singular point, G := the deck group, and the developing map becomes a bijection; transport X's topology by it (GX.ThinCex.hasAutContinuousTamifying_XA).
